name: Bus Trip to Canada Welcomes Modi Ji
location: Round-trip school bus from Durham Region
description: Ride with HCCD on a round-trip school bus to the Canada Welcomes Modi Ji event. $12.50 per person both ways.
detailedDescription:
HCCD is running a round-trip school bus to the Canada Welcomes Modi Ji event.

The fare is $12.50 per person, both ways. Seats go to the first 45 people who complete their e-transfer. If there is more interest, a second bus may be added at about $15 per person.

To reserve a seat, reach out to us through our Contact page.

name: Indian Independence Day Flag Raising
description: HCCD and the community celebrated India's Independence Day with a flag raising at Pat Bayly Square in Ajax.
detailedDescription:
HCCD proudly celebrated India's Independence Day with a flag raising ceremony at Pat Bayly Square in Ajax.

The celebration was attended by Pickering MP Juanita Nathan, Ajax MPP Rob Cerjanec, and members of the Ajax Town Council, led by Acting Deputy Mayor Sterling Lee, who proudly raised the Indian National Flag. Also joining were Marlene Crawford, Nancy Henry, Deputy Chief Chirag Bhatt, and Rob Taylor, along with members of the community.

It was a proud and memorable moment for HCCD and the entire Indian community in Durham Region. The remarkable turnout on a working day reflected the strong connection that Indians living in Ajax and surrounding communities maintain with their motherland, their heritage, and the values of freedom and unity. This landmark event marked a significant milestone in celebrating India's Independence Day in Ajax.

name: Ganesh Visarjan
description: Join HCCD at Alex Robertson Park for Ganesh Visarjan, a community celebration marking the culmination of Ganesh Chaturthi.
detailedDescription:
HCCD invites the community to Alex Robertson Park in Pickering for Ganesh Visarjan, marking the conclusion of the Ganesh Chaturthi festivities.

This event is free and open to the public.

name: Ajax–Durham Diwali Festival
location: J. Clarke Richardson Collegiate, 1355 Harwood Ave N, Ajax, ON
description: More than 3,500 people joined HCCD for Durham Region's first large-scale Diwali festival, with live performances and a spectacular drone show.
detailedDescription:
Diwali, the Festival of Lights, celebrates the victory of light over darkness and good over evil. On October 24, 2026, the Hindu Community Centre of Durham (HCCD) proudly organized the first-ever large-scale Diwali Festival featuring a spectacular drone show in the Durham Region, bringing together more than 3,500 people for an unforgettable celebration of culture, community, and togetherness.

The event attracted an impressive gathering of community members, elected officials, dignitaries, law enforcement representatives, cultural organizations, businesses, and families from across Durham Region and beyond.

We were honoured by the presence of:
• The Mayors of Ajax and Pickering
• Town and City Councillors and Regional Councillors
• Members of Parliament representing Ajax and Pickering
• Durham Regional Police Service (DRPS) Chief, Deputy Chief, Inspectors, Sergeants, and numerous police officers and constables, who attended voluntarily to support the celebration
• Representatives from the Consulate General of India
• The Honourable Consul General of Guyana

The evening featured live cultural performances, energetic DJ entertainment, and culminated in a breathtaking drone show that illuminated the night sky.

We are grateful to our corporate partners, including Ontario Power Generation (OPG), Costco, Escon, HSS, and ISA Foundations, along with several other community organizations that joined hands to make this celebration possible. Our heartfelt appreciation goes to our generous event sponsors, Ajax Crematorium and Visitation Centre and Advisory Money, whose support played an instrumental role in bringing this ambitious event to life.

Most importantly, the entire event was conducted peacefully and safely, with zero incidents reported. Everything was exceptionally well coordinated, from the performances and vendor arrangements to crowd management, security, and the drone presentation.

A sincere THANK YOU to every sponsor, partner, dignitary, volunteer, performer, vendor, law enforcement representative, and attendee who contributed to this historic success. Together, we made history in Durham Region!

name: Navratri Garba Night
location: Pickering High School, 180 Church St N, Ajax, ON, L1T 2W7
description: HCCD's first-ever Navratri Garba welcomed more than 400 people for an evening of Garba, Dandiya and devotional music at Pickering High School.
detailedDescription:
Navratri is one of the most important and widely celebrated Hindu festivals. The word Navratri means "nine nights" in Sanskrit. The festival celebrates the victory of good over evil and honours Goddess Durga, the divine feminine power (Shakti), in her various forms. During these nine nights, devotees worship Goddess Durga and her nine manifestations, seeking her blessings for strength, courage, prosperity, wisdom, and protection.

One of the most beautiful traditions of Navratri is Garba and Dandiya Raas, traditional Gujarati folk dances performed in circles with colourful traditional attire and devotional music. Today, Garba has become a global cultural celebration, bringing together people of different generations and backgrounds.

On October 17, 2026, HCCD proudly organized its first-ever Navratri Garba celebration at Pickering High School. The event welcomed more than 400 participants, along with several vendors, sponsors, volunteers, and community organizations, for an evening of traditional Garba, Dandiya, devotional music, and cultural performances. Live music was performed by singer Jitendra Joshi and his team from Malhaar Entertainment.

We were especially honoured by the presence and support of:
• Juanita Nathan, Member of Parliament for Pickering
• Jennifer McKelvie, Member of Parliament for Ajax
• Rob Cerjanec, Member of Provincial Parliament for Ajax
• Kevin Ashe, Mayor of Pickering
• Marlene Crawford, Mayor of Ajax
• Several Town, City, and Regional Councillors
• Deputy Chief Chirag Bhatt of Durham Regional Police Service (DRPS), with police Sergeants and Inspectors

The celebration was about much more than dancing. It was about preserving our religious traditions, passing our cultural heritage to younger generations, bringing families together, and giving people from diverse backgrounds the chance to experience Hindu culture.

Our heartfelt THANK YOU to everyone who participated, supported, sponsored, volunteered, and helped make this event a grand success.

name: International Yoga Day Celebration
description: HCCD's first International Yoga Day, held with Hindu Swayamsevak Sangh at Paulynn Park, brought hundreds together for yoga, sports and free food.
detailedDescription:
International Yoga Day is celebrated every year on June 21 around the world to recognize the importance of yoga in promoting physical fitness, mental well-being, mindfulness, and a balanced lifestyle. Yoga is an ancient Indian tradition that has become a global practice.

On June 21, 2026, HCCD proudly organized its first-ever International Yoga Day celebration under the HCCD banner, in collaboration with the Hindu Swayamsevak Sangh (HSS), at Paulynn Park in Ajax. The event brought together hundreds of participants, volunteers, families, community leaders, and dignitaries.

Professional yoga instructors led traditional yoga practices, breathing exercises, meditation, and even Laughter Yoga, encouraging people of all ages and fitness levels to make yoga part of their everyday lives.

Alongside Yoga Day, HSS organized Khel Divas, a sports and physical activity celebration that encourages teamwork, discipline, fitness, and leadership. Hundreds of volunteers and participants joined the sporting activities.

Paulynn Park is a community park adopted by HCCD. As part of our commitment to the environment, HCCD helps maintain the park and keep it clean, welcoming, and green for future generations.

We were honoured by the presence of:
• Juanita Nathan, Member of Parliament for Pickering
• Rob Cerjanec, Member of Provincial Parliament for Ajax
• Marlene Crawford, Mayor of Ajax
• Nancy Henry, community leader
• Councillor Ranjith and several other elected representatives and distinguished guests

Free food and refreshments were served to all participants, made possible by supporting vendors and dedicated volunteers.

Our heartfelt appreciation goes to Hindu Swayamsevak Sangh, the yoga instructors, volunteers, sponsors, food partners, elected representatives, and everyone who participated.

name: Trip to Niagara Falls for Seniors
description: A beautiful day trip to Niagara Falls with our senior community members, full of scenic views, good food, and lasting memories.
detailedDescription:
HCCD organized a wonderful day trip to Niagara Falls for our senior community members, providing a safe, comfortable, and joyful outing for all participants.

The group departed early in the morning by chartered bus and arrived at one of Canada's most iconic landmarks in time for a scenic walk along the Niagara Parkway. Highlights included breathtaking views of the Horseshoe Falls, and several stops to temples in the GTA who were kind enough to provide food!.

The event was organized with accessibility in mind, with volunteers on hand throughout the day to assist seniors as needed. Laughter, stories, and new friendships made this trip truly memorable.

We thank all volunteers, sponsors, and participants who made this special outing possible.

name: Summer Outdoor Community Event
description: A lively outdoor gathering for the whole family with cultural performances, games, and traditional food at Greenwood Community Centre.
detailedDescription:
Our Summer Outdoor Community Event brought together families and friends from across the Durham Region for an afternoon of cultural celebration, fun, and togetherness.

The event featured live classical Indian music and dance performances, traditional folk games for children and adults alike, and a vibrant marketplace of homemade food, sweets, and crafts. Community members showcased their talents on stage while families relaxed on the lawn and connected with one another.

Highlights included a mehndi (henna) corner, a children's activity zone, and a communal dinner featuring dishes from across the Indian subcontinent.

Over 300 attendees joined us on a beautiful summer afternoon. It was a true celebration of community!
